title: An adaptable live-cell imaging protocol to analyze organelle morphology in Saccharomyces cerevisiae
protocol: Inoculate a single colony of yeast in appropriate synthetic minimal or complete media.
Grow the inoculated culture overnight (12–14 hours) at 30°C with shaking at 220 rpm.
Sub-culture into fresh medium to achieve an initial OD600 of 0.15–0.2 and continue growing for 3–4 hours at 30°C with shaking at 220 rpm.
Harvest cells from mid-log phase (OD600- 0.6 to 1.0) by spinning 1 mL of culture at 3000g for 1 minute.
Wash the pellet with 1 mL of fresh media prewarmed to the growth temperature (usually 30°C).
Resuspend the pellet in 20–50 μL of media.
Immobilize the cells using a glass bottom dish coated with 0.1% ConA.
Lay 10 μL cell suspension over the ConA-coated dish and spread gently with P200 pipette tip.
Let the cells adhere by leaving undisturbed for 3-5 minutes.
Add 500 μL of media and mix up and down gently using a pipette to remove unadhered cells.
Remove excess liquid and repeat the process two more times.
Add 500 μL - 1 mL of fresh media and begin imaging.
For higher cell density, use a larger volume of cell suspension.
To reduce cell density, dilute the cell suspension or increase washing steps.
Place the dish on the stage after adding immersion oil to the objective.
Focus on a field of cells.
Start with a low cell density field for time lapse imaging (3–5 cells/50 μm × 50 μm).
Visualize the signal for the fluorophore of interest.
Use a low imaging format (512 × 512 or 1024 × 1024) and high scan speed (400 Hz or 600 Hz) during visualization.
Set the laser intensity and detector gain.
Observe the signal.
Start scanning with low laser power (0.5%–2%) and increase further based on the signal.
Follow the image histogram to check the dynamic range and ensure that the signal is not saturated.
Switch to ‘Quick lookup table’ mode to highlight saturated regions when using Leica equipment.
Ensure that the cells have adhered properly and there are no floating cells in the field of view.
Repeat cell immobilization steps until optimum density is obtained if the field of view is crowded with cells or cells are layered.
Avoid fields populated with too many cells at the start of a time course of live cell imaging.
Check for bacterial contamination by focusing on potential bacteria under the microscope and ensure the background is clear.
Deconvolve the images using Huygens Professional or appropriate deconvolution tools.
Export the images to Huygens Professionals for further analysis.
View the thumbnail of exported images in the software window for initial assessment.
Check the image quality before starting deconvolution.
View Nyquist parameters for the selected image.
Right-click on the selected image and select deconvolution wizard.
If the image acquisition parameters are not optimum, use another image with higher format and better resolution.
Estimate background using in/near object estimation mode.
Use GMLE (Good’s roughness Maximum Likelihood Estimation) deconvolution algorithm for deconvolution.
Set signal to noise ratio (SNR) between 10–14 based on fluorophore intensity.
Deconvolve images iteratively based on PSF.
Open the image file in FIJI.
Use the freehand tool in FIJI to draw over the nuclear outline.
Select the circularity measurement from the Set Measurement window.
Measure the perimeter, area and volume of each nucleus using the Analyze tool of FIJI.
Adjust the pixel width of the line depending on the structure that is traced.
Select the ‘Freehand selections’ tool.
Go to the Edit menu and click on Options.
Enter the appropriate value for thickness.
Carefully select the z section before drawing the ROI over the NE.
Ensure that the maximum nuclear perimeter lies in the selected z-plane.
Mark each nucleus individually.
Add the selection to the ROI manager (Press T or go to Edit → Selection→Add to Manager).
Tick the ‘Label’ box in the ROI manager dialog box to avoid marking the same nuclei multiple times.
Exclude dividing cells, cells with entire nucleus not covered in the stack, and cells at the edges of the field when marking nuclei.
Extract line profiles for multiple regions of interest (ROIs) using the ROI manager.
Click on More, followed by Multi Plot to extract intensity profiles.
Compare intensity profiles from at least 10 to 15 cells from 3 independent experiments.
Quantify intensity-based differences as an aggregation index or a function of variation in intensity along the ROI.
